Daily Brief

The day's most consequential developments center on cautious optimism in the US-Iran conflict, with President Trump announcing ongoing negotiations after three days without strikes, while warning the US would resume attacks if talks fail [BBC, France 24]. Oil prices fell sharply on de-escalation hopes. In Europe, catastrophic wildfires continue ravaging France and Spain, with over 325,000 evacuated and temperatures forecast to rise again [RFI, BBC, Financial Times]. The fires near Bordeaux have burned 42,000 hectares and generated unprecedented fire-weather phenomena. French football received significant news as Zinedine Zidane was confirmed as the new Les Bleus head coach, replacing Didier Deschamps [France 24]. Meanwhile, Italy's football federation was thrown into crisis after Andrea Pirlo withdrew from consideration for the national team role over ties to a Russian betting firm, prompting resignations from senior officials [BBC Europe]. A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck Japan's Kyushu region, triggering tsunami warnings across multiple prefectures [The Hindu]. Johnson & Johnson offered up to $5.5 billion to settle tens of thousands of talc-related cancer lawsuits in the US [BBC].

01 Conflict

US and Iran Pause Strikes as Trump Signals Optimism on Negotiations

  • US and Iran have not exchanged strikes for three consecutive days following nearly two weeks of daily US attacks aimed at degrading Iran's ability to threaten shipping in the Strait of Hormuz
  • Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One that 'friendly negotiations' are underway through mediators and expressed optimism that 'something could happen,' while warning strikes would resume if talks fail
  • Tehran denied direct negotiations are taking place but acknowledged mediators are conveying messages; Iran has also halted its attacks during the pause
  • Oil prices fell more than 9% to $87.59 per barrel on Monday amid hopes of de-escalation

03 Society

Zinedine Zidane Named Head Coach of French National Football Team

  • Zinedine Zidane will be officially announced as Les Bleus coach by French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo on Tuesday
  • Zidane, 54, has not coached since leaving Real Madrid in 2021, where he led the club to three consecutive Champions League titles (2016-2018)
  • He replaces Didier Deschamps, who stepped down after France lost to Spain in the 2026 World Cup semifinals
  • More than 120 journalists and photographers expected at FFF headquarters for the announcement

04 Society

Italy Football Crisis Deepens as Pirlo Withdraws Over Russian Betting Ties

  • Andrea Pirlo withdrew his candidacy for Italy head coach after criticism over his role as global ambassador for Russian betting company Fonbet since October 2025
  • Fonbet has sponsored sporting events involving veterans of Russia's war in Ukraine and hosted events where Pirlo appeared alongside pro-Kremlin figures
  • Technical director Paolo Maldini and adviser Leonardo resigned following Pirlo's withdrawal, deepening the federation's crisis
  • Italy has failed to qualify for three successive World Cups; politicians argued anyone promoting Russia since 2022 should not hold national office

Magnitude 7.1 Earthquake Strikes Japan's Kyushu, Triggering Tsunami Warning

  • A 7.1 magnitude earthquake struck Kumamoto prefecture on Japan's southern Kyushu island on Tuesday
  • Japan Meteorological Agency issued a tsunami warning for waves measuring 1 meter
  • Emergency earthquake warnings issued for seven prefectures: Kumamoto, Nagasaki, Kagoshima, Fukuoka, Saga, Oita, and Miyazaki
